historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (guidance-anchored). The equity 5yr CAGR of 10.0% was rejected as the forward proxy: it embeds the April-2024 MDC acquisition (revenue +31% in FY2024, debt x2.5) and JPY213bn of yen-translation gains in AOCI, neither of which is organic compounding.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr), fiscal years ending 31 January of the following calendar year. Owner FCF series (OCF - PP&E capex - intangibles capex where disclosed) is FY2020 104,482; FY2021 35,083; FY2022 33,302; FY2023 -61,254; FY2024 -28,121; FY2025 121,237 - dominated by real-estate inventory investment (FY2023-24 land bank +JPY1.0tn incl. MDC), so the FCF CAGRs are noise, not trend: the 3yr figure is a low-base artefact and the 5yr 3.0% compares two peak-conversion years. Owner FCF has averaged 54% of attributable net income over FY2021-25; the DCF's negative working-capital capture is what carries that gap forward. SBC is nil so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs coincide.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's FY2026 numbers (sales +1.5%, OP 350bn) are met, then the two axes that decide Sekisui House's next decade both move moderately: (1) US homebuilding - Sekisui House U.S. (MDC/Richmond American + Woodside + Chesmar + Holt, one company since January 2026, #6 US builder) recovers from the FY2025 operating loss as mortgage rates ease and incentives fade, taking overseas OP from 39bn toward the 56bn guided and beyond; (2) Japan - new housing starts keep shrinking ~1-2%/yr but rental housing management (713bn, 9.7% margin, growing 3-4%), remodeling and urban redevelopment lift the mix. Revenue compounds ~3%/yr to ~5.4tn by FY2035, EBITDA margin reaches 10%, and the land bank is turned rather than grown (WC consumes 60% of each yen of incremental revenue). Leverage falls gradually toward the MTP's soundness target; the 145-yen dividend floor is comfortably covered by owner FCF of ~150-250bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: US demand recovers with lower rates and the one-company integration delivers the cost/land synergies the MDC deal was justified on: US homebuilding margins return to mid-to-high single digits, overseas revenue grows high single digits, and the 7th MTP's high-12% ROE is reached by FY2028 (EBITDA ~11%). Japan's Development and urban-redevelopment pipeline (Grand Green Osaka etc.) delivers, and a move to lot options in the US improves inventory turnover (WC -50%). The company resumes buybacks as leverage normalises. Terminal value is still capped at 15x FCF - the bull is a margin and growth story, not a re-rating story.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2025 US margin collapse was the start of a cycle, not a blip: affordability stays stretched, incentives and tariff-driven cost inflation keep US homebuilding at or below break-even through FY2027, and a land bank bought at 2021-24 prices (overseas inventory 2.45tn, 1.9x overseas revenue) takes further valuation losses. Japan's Development segment normalises from an unusually strong FY2025 and starts fall faster on demographics and the post-Energy-Act hangover. Consolidated revenue dips in FY2027, EBITDA troughs at 7.8%, and the post-MDC balance sheet (net debt ~3.7x EBITDA) means deleveraging rather than returns absorbs the cash. The firm survives easily - the bear is a decade of ~2% growth at 8% margins while carrying the inventory.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sekisui House screens cheap on earnings (P/E ~10x, P/B ~1.0x, 4% dividend yield) but a homebuilder-developer's earnings are not its free cash flow: FY2021-25 owner FCF was 54% of net income because every yen of growth is pre-funded by land and buildings for sale, now JPY3.2tn. This DCF charges that inventory investment explicitly (negative working-capital capture), charges the MDC acquisition debt once in the bridge, adds back the investment-securities portfolio whose income is excluded from the flows, and caps the exit at 15x owner FCF so no re-rating is assumed. The result is a value that depends mostly on whether US homebuilding margins recover and on how much capital the growth consumes - the two axes the scenarios span. A 7% JPY WACC is used in all scenarios; risk is in the flows and weights, not stacked in the rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: US housing cycle: mortgage-rate and incentive trajectory drives ~40% of the swing in consolidated operating profit; FY2025 US homebuilding was loss-making
Inventory valuation: JPY3.2tn of land/buildings for sale (overseas 2.45tn) is exposed to write-downs; FY2024-25 evaluation losses were 17.5bn and 19.8bn
Working-capital intensity assumption (-60% capture) is the single largest driver of owner FCF; a land-light US model would add materially, a land-heavy one subtract
Leverage: net debt JPY1.46tn (~3.7x EBITDA) after MDC; interest expense 39bn/yr; deleveraging competes with the 145-yen dividend floor and buybacks
USD/JPY translation: ~31% of revenue is USD/AUD; a 10% yen appreciation cuts reported overseas revenue by ~130bn
Japan demographics: new housing starts in secular decline, capping the legacy custom-detached and rental-construction segments
Terminal multiple: 15x cap binds in all three scenarios; the market has paid 9-11x earnings for this stock for a decade, so even the house exit multiple assumes no discount for cyclicality

inputs.share_count_basis: 651,585,566 issued less 3,182,159 treasury at 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2026 tanshin, cover page) = 648.40m; 11.7m treasury shares were cancelled in March 2026 (FY2025 tanshin note 'Cancellation of Treasury Stock'), which changes issued but not outstanding. Share acquisition rights are JPY53m (de minimis), so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is nil, buybacks are a value-neutral mechanism here; FY2024-25 buyback cash was JPY14-18m (nil), after JPY30-40bn/yr in FY2022-23.
inputs.debt_composition: At 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2026 tanshin BS): short-term borrowings 394,312 + current LT borrowings 229,366 + bonds 754,779 + LT borrowings 503,842 = 1,882,299. No short-term bonds/CP outstanding. Cash and deposits 427,080. Jan-2026 equivalents were 1,848,889 / 435,177 (ties to Metrics.csv).
inputs.sbc_source: J-GAAP filer; no share-based compensation expense disclosed in FY2011-FY2025 tanshin or annual reports. Share acquisition rights on the balance sheet are JPY53-87m. SBC-zero market: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position is null.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-26T02:30:00Z (11:30 JST, intraday TSE print, not a close; 52-week range 3181-3832)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity 9.0% = 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.2 x JPY ERP 6.0% (beta above market because ~31% of sales and the main profit swing are US homebuilding, where listed peers carry betas of 1.3-1.5). After-tax cost of debt 1.6% (FY2025 interest expense 39,183 / average interest-bearing debt ~1.85tn = 2.1% pre-tax, x 0.7). Weights at the 7th-MTP TARGET structure, D/V 30% (management's 'restoration of financial soundness' goal), not today's post-MDC gross leverage of ~44%, because using the acquisition-inflated debt weight would reward leverage with a lower discount rate. 0.7 x 9.0 + 0.3 x 1.6 = 6.8%, carried as 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, US-housing and integration risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP: operating leases are expensed in opex, so no IFRS-16 adjustment is needed. Finance-lease assets of JPY38.8bn sit in PP&E with obligations inside 'Other' liabilities (<1% of EV) and are left out of net debt; their cost is in the EBITDA path. Treatment (B)-equivalent, consistent with Metrics.csv total_debt which excludes leases.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated EBITDA (include the ~2% NCI share of profit, JPY4.5bn FY2025); the NCI stock of JPY53,451m at 2026-07-31 is deducted once, in the equity bridge. FY0 check: EBIT 341,402 x 0.70 = 239k unlevered NOPAT vs attributable NI 232,095 + after-tax interest ~27k - after-tax equity-method/securities gains ~27k = ~232k; ties within non-operating noise.
inputs.working_capital_treatment: Real estate for sale (land, lots, buildings) was JPY3,176bn at 2026-07-31, 0.72x revenue (overseas inventory JPY2,450bn is 1.9x overseas revenue; Japan JPY726bn is 0.25x). Net of advances received (269bn) and construction payables (227bn), net operating working capital is ~0.66x revenue. Inventory growth is this developer's real growth capital and has held OCF to 54% of net income over FY2021-25, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE: -60% of the revenue change in the base (-50% bull: US lot-option/land-light shift and faster turnover; -70% bear: slower absorption, land held longer). The 7th MTP's JPY5.6tn FY2026-28 investment plan (3.75tn overseas) against ~1.6tn/yr cost of sales implies the land bank is being turned rather than grown, consistent with -60%.
inputs.capex_treatment: Capex here is purchases of PP&E PLUS intangibles (FY2025: 66,930 + 28,158 = 95,088, 2.27% of revenue; Metrics.csv 'CapEx' and FCF carry PP&E only, so owner FCF subtracts the intangibles line separately). FY2026 plan ~JPY110bn (2.6%). D&A (42,761, 1.02%) runs well below capex because the Development business builds owned rental/commercial property; D&A path rises as that base grows.
inputs.equity_bridge_rationale: Matching-asset rule: dividend income (2.2bn), equity-method profit (26.1bn, lumpy; Singapore/US/Australia JVs) and securities gains (12.4bn) sit below operating profit and are excluded from the EBITDA-based flows, so investment securities (JPY192,528m at 2026-07-31, including equity-method investments at book and AFS securities at fair value) are added in the bridge. The JPY112.9bn retirement benefit asset and JPY23bn long-term loans receivable are NOT added (not realisable to shareholders in practice). NCI deducted as above.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (JPY, SBC-zero, non-US adaptations applied: currency-matched WACC, single lease treatment, NCI once, matching-asset bridge, negative working-capital capture). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'; Sekisui House is an operating homebuilder/developer, not a REIT, bank or land-only subdivider: ~61% of revenue is contract building, rental management and remodeling, so the FCF engine applies with inventory handled as working capital rather than switching to the NTA/P-E blend. Fresh build, no prior DCF. FY0 is FY2025 = year ended 2026-01-31 (Sekisui labels the fiscal year by its START calendar year). Year-1 (FY2026, ending 2027-01-31) is anchored to the guidance revised on 2026-09-10 with the Q2 results: net sales JPY4,260bn (+1.5%, cut from 4,353bn), operating profit JPY350bn (+2.5%, unchanged), ordinary profit 316bn, attributable profit 224bn (raised from 218bn), EPS 345.55, DPS 145 (floor through FY2028). H1 FY2026 operating profit was already +16% (180.4bn, 9.2% OP margin), so the full-year 350bn implies a soft H2 and looks conservative; the base holds management's number, the bull gives credit for it. last_fcf (121,237) = reported FCF 149,395 - intangibles capex 28,158; it is post interest paid (38,632, inside J-GAAP operating cash flow) whereas the projection is unlevered, so year-1 modelled FCF (~146bn) is comparable to last_fcf plus ~27bn after-tax interest. Interest income (5,999) is NOT stripped: the company is a large net borrower (net debt ~3.7x EBITDA), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. Price is an intraday TSE print; replace at the next regular close if it has moved. The 15% hurdle is the house standard; in JPY with a 1.7% risk-free rate it is a very demanding bar and the required-return table is the more useful reading.

bear.narrative: US housing downturn: incentives rise, inventory write-downs recur (FY2025 US homebuilding already lost JPY5.3bn), overseas OP turns negative in FY2027; Japan starts keep falling and Development normalises from the FY2025 peak; EBITDA troughs at 7.8% and recovers only to 8%; land bank turns slowly (WC -70%). Capex is cut but the inventory still has to be carried. No solvency event - interest cover stays >5x.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = revised guidance +1.5%. FY2027-28 +4% as US closings recover from the FY2025-26 trough and the 7th MTP's overseas investment converts to deliveries; then decelerating to 1.5% as Japan housing starts (secular decline, ~800k/yr) offset US growth.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA 9.3% = guided OP 350bn + ~46bn D&A on 4,260bn. Ramps to 10.0% by FY2031 on US homebuilding margin normalising from ~0% toward mid-single digits and the mix shift to rental management/remodeling (mid-teens margins). Deliberately below the ~11% EBITDA the MTP's high-12% ROE target implies for FY2028.
base.tax_rationale: 30% cash rate: Japan statutory ~30.6%, US ~25%; FY2025 GAAP effective 30.2%, cash paid 25.8% (timing), FY2026 plan 31.3%.
base.terminal_rationale: g 1.0% (Japan nominal growth ~1%, shrinking new-build volumes, US adds). Cap 15x owner FCF binds over Gordon (1.01/0.06 = 16.8x) - a cyclical developer should not be capitalised above a mid-teens FCF multiple.

bull.narrative: US mortgage rates ease, Sekisui House U.S. (one entity since Jan-2026) lifts closings and margins toward the MTP, Japan mix shifts to recurring; EBITDA reaches the ~11% the high-12% ROE target implies; lot-option/land-light shift lowers WC intensity to -50%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: this is a highly cyclical business whose profit swing is now US homebuilding (operating loss in FY2025), carrying JPY1.88tn of acquisition debt (net debt ~3.7x EBITDA) and a JPY3.2tn real-estate inventory exposed to write-downs - the bear case is a plausible cycle, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: US rates easing, the four-brand integration delivering margins, Japan's redevelopment pipeline landing on time, and a shift to land-light US operations. Base holds 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
